content: Warnings This vaginal cream contains mineral oil, which has the potential to weaken latex or rubber-based products, such as condoms or vaginal contraceptive diaphragms. As a result, it is advised to avoid using such products within 72 hours after treatment with GYNAZOLE-1® Butoconazole Nitrate Vaginal Cream USP, 2%. Women who experience recurrent vaginal yeast infections, particularly those that are resistant to treatment, should be evaluated for potential underlying conditions. In women at risk for HIV infection, recurrent yeast infections may serve as an early indicator of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection. Precautions General If clinical symptoms persist after treatment, further diagnostic testing should be conducted. This includes ruling out other pathogens, confirming the initial diagnosis, and identifying any underlying conditions that may predispose the patient to recurrent vaginal fungal infections. Carcinogenesis Long-term studies in animals have not been conducted to assess the potential for this drug to cause cancer. Mutagenicity Butoconazole nitrate has been evaluated in various mutagenicity tests, including the Ames bacterial test, yeast assays, chromosomal aberration assays in CHO cells, CHO/HGPRT point mutation assays, mouse micronucleus tests, and rat dominant lethal assays. In all these tests, butoconazole nitrate did not demonstrate mutagenic properties. Impairment of Fertility Studies in rabbits and rats have shown no evidence of impaired fertility when butoconazole nitrate was administered orally at doses up to 30 mg/kg/day in rabbits (equivalent to 5 times the human dose based on body surface area) and 100 mg/kg/day in rats (equivalent to 10 times the human dose based on body surface area). Pregnancy Butoconazole nitrate is classified as Pregnancy Category C. In studies involving pregnant rats, intravaginal administration of 6 mg/kg/day during organogenesis resulted in an increased rate of fetal resorption and a reduction in litter size, though no teratogenic effects were observed. This dose represents a safety margin of 130 to 353 times the serum levels achieved in humans following intravaginal administration of the recommended therapeutic dose. When administered orally to pregnant rats during organogenesis at doses up to 50 mg/kg/day (5 times the human dose based on body surface area), no adverse effects were observed. However, higher oral doses of 100, 300, or 750 mg/kg/day (10, 30, or 75 times the human dose, respectively) resulted in fetal malformations, such as abdominal wall defects and cleft palate. These effects were accompanied by signs of maternal stress at these higher dose levels. In rabbits, no adverse effects on litters were observed, even at maternally stressful oral doses of 150 mg/kg/day (24 times the human dose based on body surface area). Like other azole antifungal agents, butoconazole nitrate has been shown to cause dystocia (difficult labor) in rats when treatment is extended through parturition. However, this effect was not observed in rabbits treated with oral doses as high as 100 mg/kg/day (16 times the human dose based on body surface area). There are no adequate and well-controlled studies of butoconazole nitrate use in pregnant women. Therefore, GYNAZOLE-1® Butoconazole Nitrate Vaginal Cream USP, 2% should only be used during pregnancy if the potential benefits to the mother outweigh the potential risks to the fetus. Nursing Mothers It is not known whether butoconazole nitrate is excreted in human breast milk. Given that many drugs are excreted in breast milk, caution is advised when administering butoconazole nitrate to nursing mothers. Pediatric Use The safety and effectiveness of butoconazole nitrate in pediatric patients have not been established.
